references.text: The people also grumbled against Moses in the Desert of Sin due to lack of food, showing a pattern of complaining against Moses during the wilderness journey.
A similar incident where the people quarreled with Moses over water at Meribah and complained about the lack of water in the wilderness.
Moses warns the people not to test the Lord as they did at Massah, a direct reference to this event.
The psalm mentions Meribah and Massah as places where the ancestors tested God and put him to the test.
God tested the people at the waters of Meribah, a poetic reference to this incident.
The place was called Massah and Meribah because of the quarreling of the Israelites and because they tested the Lord.
Hebrews quotes Psalm 95 and warns against hardening the heart as in the temptation in the wilderness, where the ancestors tested God.
Paul warns against testing Christ just as some of the ancestors did in the wilderness, referencing the trials of the wilderness journey.
Jesus quotes Deuteronomy 6:16 when he rejects Satan's temptation, indirectly referring to the incident at Massah.
The immediate precursor to the conflict at Rephidim; shows a recurring pattern of complaining against Moses and God's leadership.
A theological contrast: here the people test the Lord without repenting, while later they admit their sin and ask for prayer.
Theological reflection: in one verse the people put God to the test, in the other God tests the people for their obedience.
Direct parallel: both incidents involve a lack of water and use the phrase 'to test the Lord' (Marah vs. Rephidim).
Theological parallel: both verses emphasize that grumbling against Moses is actually a confrontation with the Lord.
